title: Don't give up meeting (Hebrews 10:19–25)
hookLine: draw near; hold fast; stir each other up to love
tomorrow: how do you pack for a trip when nobody tells you where?

lines: A SERVICE ON A TRAY TABLE.
AS THE MANNER OF SOME IS.
cards: A tablet propped on a hospital tray table, the church service streaming, the choir a half-second out of sync with the picture. If you can pray anywhere, why does Hebrews care who shows up?
Because some had already stopped. The letter says so, almost in passing: "Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is." As the manner of some is.
Empty seats, already. The writer doesn't name anyone or scold them. Instead comes a reason, and it has nothing to do with taking attendance.

teach.b: First the passage opens a door: "Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, By a new and living way." Then three invitations, each starting let us.
"Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith." "Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering."
And the third turns sideways, toward each other: "And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works." Provoke is usually the word for starting a fight. Here it's aimed at love.
So does showing up in person still matter? Christians hold two honest views.

teach.h: VIEW ONE: BODIES IN ONE ROOM.
teach.b: The first: yes, bodies in one room. You can't consider someone you never see. A gathered church shares bread, sings out loud, and notices who's missing, and people who hold this view point to the word itself: assembling.
The second: the gathering is wherever believers meet in his name.

teach.h: VIEW TWO: WHERE TWO OR THREE GATHER.
teach.b: Jesus says, "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them."
For the sick, the homebound and the far away, people who hold this view say a kitchen table or a hospital room is a real gathering.
Here's what both sides keep: the reason for meeting is each other, "exhorting one another," which means encouraging.

how: Christians gather for worship, often weekly, and churches also bring prayer and communion to people who are sick or homebound; some also worship together online.

games.q: what does “don't give up meeting” mean?
o: keep every appointment you make with friends
keep gathering so you can stir each other to love
never miss a Sunday, or you lose your place

p: as the manner of some is

s: provoke in Hebrews 10:24 means making someone angry
here it's aimed the other way: to provoke unto love and to good works.
Hebrews names and scolds the people who stopped coming
it names no one. it says as the manner of some is, and gives a reason to gather.
the passage says some had already stopped gathering
not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is.

games.q: your friend says she worships online now and doesn't miss the building at all. you lean the other way. what's the best case for HER view?
o: where two or three are gathered, he is there; a screen can hold that.
Hebrews says the building matters less than private prayer.
online is easier, and easier is what Hebrews asks for.
games.why: that's her side at its strongest: Jesus' promise in Matthew 18:20. the in-person view answers: you can't consider someone you never see. both are Christian voices.

practice: Bring to mind one person who used to show up, at church, at practice, in a group chat, and has gone quiet. Write them a short message with no guilt in it, only glad you exist.
Hold it through the sit, and send it when it feels right.

wordCard.voice: Don't give up meeting. Hebrews ten: draw near, hold fast, and keep gathering, so you can stir one another up to love.

orig.note: Greek: a stirring up; the word behind provoke in Hebrews 10:24.

carryVoice: The line to keep: stir up love, provoke aimed the other way for once. Go well.
